thread.title: US Dollar Strong Ahead of NFP as the Pound Plunges after BoE Rate Hike

author: James Elliot
title: US Dollar Strong Ahead of NFP as the Pound Plunges after BoE Rate Hike
text:
US Dollar Strong Ahead Of NFP As The Pound Plunges After BoE Rate Hike US Dollar Strong Ahead Of NFP As The Pound Plunges After BoE Rate Hike Facebook NFP is the big event on Friday. While the data may cause short-term volatility, the US dollar has other drivers. The British Pound found no support after the BoE raised rates.
The US dollar keeps pushing higher ahead of Friday’s US jobs report and it would take a surprising miss of the 190k estimate to reverse the weekly gains. Even this would be unlikely to cause a full reversal of the underlying uptrend in the dollar or change expectations for a further two rate hikes this year. Unemployment is likely to hover around 4%, and could even dip below later this year. Only a sustained worsening of the labour market would have any bearing on the longer-term dollar moves.
As SEB wrote in their preview note,
“Wednesday's ADP positively surprised and yesterday's statistics on new/existing jobless claims were close to historical bottom levels. We believe that today's NFP figure lands slightly below consensus (180k, consensus 193k) which is also somewhat below last month's 213k. The average hourly earnings are still in focus for the Fed and we expect them to have increased by 0.3% m/m and 2.7% y/y which would indicate a continued moderate upturn. However, we expect earnings to rise further ahead driven by the strong labour market.”
Any trend change in the dollar is therefore unlikely to come from worsening jobs data. A strong outlook for the economy was also underlined by the Fed this week in Wednesday’s rate meeting, and if there was any doubt of the bullish sentiment, Apple (AAPL) beat earnings estimates and rallied to become the world’s first ever trillion market cap stock. Assuming the S&P500 holds its gains into the end of the week, it will post its 5th positive week in a row, which is the best run this year. Things couldn’t be better for America.
Yet the strength in the dollar and overly bullish sentiment could be its undoing. President Trump has made it clear he does not support a stronger dollar and any break to new highs is likely to be met with criticism. The market is also overly long so any unexpected negatives for the dollar could have an exaggerated effect. Pound Plunges on Rate Hike
The Bank of England raised rates at Thursday’s meeting for only the second time since the financial crisis. This was broadly expected, but by no means guaranteed. However, there were two surprises of note.
Firstly, the vote for a rate rise was a unanimous 9-0, when most expected at least one dissenter, and the consensus was for a 7-2 vote. And while it is reasonable to say this was a “dovish” hike, it was not as dovish as many may have expected. The bank expects a slightly higher rate of growth in the medium term, and while there were the customary references to Brexit and trade tensions to cover any risks to the downside, the outlook was bullish.
The second surprise came from the price action in GBP. Despite the rate hike and the not so dovish aspects, GBP plunged across the board. GBPUSD was especially weak and is currently trading below 1.3 and near the July lows. It seems short-term traders were long for a pop higher, but are being forced to cover lower as the pop failed to materialize.
Many are now wondering “what next?”, and as ING explain, the rate of change could be very slow.
“…the Bank has announced explicitly for the first time that it estimates the longer-term neutral rate to be 2-3%. Depending on how you look at it, this could be interpreted as a subtle prod for markets to lift their rate expectations for two-three years’ time. That’s possibly a stretch, but either way, with Brexit risks mounting, markets are unlikely to take too much notice.” Advertisement
